exercises.prompt: Vocalize the nominal sentence after إِنَّ ('Indeed, patience is the key to relief'):
exercises.explanation: إِنَّ governs its subject (ism inna) in the ACCUSATIVE (fatḥah) while leaving its predicate (مِفْتَاحُ) nominative.

feedback.rule: إِنَّ makes ism inna accusative (manṣūb) and keeps khabar inna nominative (marfūʿ).

exercises.prompt: True or False: Attaching emphatic لَـ (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqah) to khabar inna (e.g., إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَغَفُورٌ) changes its case to genitive.
exercises.explanation: False. Al-lām al-muzaḥlaqah is a particle of emphasis, not a preposition; khabar inna remains nominative (لَغَفُورٌ).

feedback.rule: Emphatic لَـ on khabar inna does not alter its nominative case.
